Florensocatib reduces exacerbations more in low-symptom patients, while inhaled tobramycin improves symptoms more in high-symptom patients. Symptom burden may serve as a simple tool for personalized therapy.

papers.title: Individualized antisense oligonucleotide treatment eligibility of patients living with neurodevelopmental diseases
papers.summary: Aartsma-Rus et al. provide a perspective on the eligibility of patients for treatment with individualized antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). Individualized ASOs are developed specifically for patients with nanorare diseases. So far, the focus has been on neurodegenerative diseases. Here, authors make a case to also consider patients with neurodevelopmental diseases.

papers.title: Exercise intensity modulates interorgan communication and is associated with cardiometabolic health outcomes in humans
papers.summary: Sprint-interval exercise (SIE) is a time-efficient exercise prescription. However, how short bursts of physical activity promote metabolic health remains unclear. Olsen et al. show that SIE stimulates greater remodeling of plasma, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue than moderate-intensity exercise, suggesting that predicted interorgan crosstalk may contribute to SIE’s metabolic benefits.

papers.title: Spatial proteogenomic profiling uncovers sensitization strategies for antibody-drug conjugate in HER2-positive breast cancer
papers.summary: Cai et al. report that high cancer-cell H3K27ac boosts antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) efficacy by promoting ERBB2 transcription in HER2-positive breast cancer, whereas collagen-positive fibroblasts cause ADC resistance. These findings suggest that combining ADC with histone deacetylase inhibitor chidamide or collagen-depleting agent losartan may augment ADC efficacy in treating HER2-positive breast cancer.

papers.title: A large language model-driven multidisciplinary AI agent system predicts delirium in emergency critically ill patients
papers.summary: Shang et al. develop DeLiriuMAgents, an LLM-driven multi-agent system for delirium risk prediction in emergency critically ill patients. DeLiriuMAgents reaches a final decision by integrating machine learning-based risk prediction; LLM-based virtual specialist reasoning in emergency medicine, neurology, and psychiatry; and medical evidence via retrieval-augmented generation.

papers.title: Cofilin1-driven cytoskeletal remodeling modulates pan-cancer CD8+ T cell immunotherapy responses
papers.summary: Li et al. establish CFL1 as a biomechanical checkpoint that licenses immune synapse formation through actin remodeling, rendering tumors vulnerable to CD8+ T cells. Tumor-targeted AAV-CFL1S3A/K22R combined with PD-1 blockade achieves near-complete eradication.

papers.title: Preclinical evaluation of nitrated α-synuclein-specific CAR-Treg therapy in Parkinson’s disease
papers.summary: Ugalde et al. develop a regulatory CAR-T cell therapy that targets nitrated α-synuclein, a disease-associated form of α-synuclein. In two Parkinson’s disease mouse models, this therapy reduces harmful α-synuclein-specific T cell responses, limits brain pathology, and improves motor function.

papers.title: Discovery of antimicrobial peptides from incomplete biosynthetic gene clusters to combat multidrug-resistant bacteria
papers.summary: Tang et al. develop an evolution-guided strategy to mine nonribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) peptides from genomic fragments, yielding five new antibacterial polymyxin analogues in Paenibacillus. Among these, NP001 effectively inhibits Gram-negative bacterial strains containing MCR-1 in vitro and in vivo, indicating that it is a promising drug candidate.

papers.title: A unified framework and benchmark for generalizable biomedical knowledge extraction and applications with large language models
papers.summary: Lan et al. present InfoFlowEX, a unified framework for generalizable biomedical knowledge extraction with large language models. By integrating 40 public datasets through ontology-guided alignment and schema instruction tuning, InfoFlowEX improves cross-task performance, supporting biomedical evidence retrieval, clinical diagnosis, and knowledge graph expansion.

papers.title: A high-resolution circulating metabolic atlas of lung adenocarcinoma progression supports early and accurate diagnosis
papers.summary: Shouzhi Yang et al. map a high-resolution circulating metabolic atlas for lung adenocarcinoma progression, developing a rapid blood test to identify pre-invasive tumors and improve diagnosis accuracy.

papers.title: Global gut microbiome atlas identifies epidemiologic-stage-specific signatures in inflammatory bowel disease
papers.summary: By integrating 117,799 gut 16S profiles from 70 countries alongside shotgun and strain-level metagenomes, Zhai et al. build a global atlas linking IBD epidemiologic stages to gut microbial ecology. They define stage-resolved microbial signatures and a 19-genus risk score (MIRS), which tracks national IBD burden in high-prevalence regions.

papers.title: Chronic interferon signaling at baseline is associated with acquired resistance to immunotherapy in metastatic melanoma
papers.summary: Egan et al. analyze pre-treatment melanoma samples from first-line immune checkpoint blockade patients. Using a tumor purity-informed model to deconvolve cancer cell signals from bulk RNA-seq, they show that chronic interferon signaling drives dedifferentiation and impaired antigen presentation in tumors that later relapse, identifying targets to prevent acquired resistance.

papers.title: Multi-modal AI-enabled steatotic liver disease diagnostics using facial images and metabolomics
papers.summary: Gao et al. present a deep learning system that uses three-dimensional facial images to non-invasively detect steatotic liver disease. The derived facial risk score reflects underlying glycolipid and amino acid metabolic alterations. Multimodal integration with metabolomics further enhances accuracy, while smartphone compatibility and privacy-preserving federated learning make population-scale screening feasible.

papers.title: Microenvironment-responsive magnesium stents for targeted atherosclerotic plaque removal and restenosis mitigation
papers.summary: Shen et al. develop a microenvironment-responsive magnesium stent that integrates nanocoating and liposomal delivery to target atherosclerotic plaques. The system modulates cholesterol metabolism, oxidative stress, and immune responses, enabling coordinated vascular remodeling and reducing restenosis across multiple in vivo models.

papers.title: Precision neoadjuvant treatment with AI-assisted subtyping in HR+/HER2−breast cancer: A randomized, phase 2 trial FASCINATE-N
papers.summary: Li et al. report findings from the FASCINATE-N trial showing that neoadjuvant precision treatment guided by SNF subtyping for patients with HR+/HER2− breast cancer exhibits potential clinical benefits, with improvement of efficacy in the targeted-based group and better tolerance in the endocrine-based group.

papers.title: Glutamine-restricted diets restore sensitivity to KRASG12D inhibitor through the reversal of ANXA1 mediated metabolic reprogramming
papers.summary: Jiatong Li et al. reveal that glutamine metabolic reprogramming drives pancreatic cancer resistance to KRASG12D inhibitors via ANXA1-mediated stabilization of GOT1 and mitochondrial translocation of GLS1. Glutamine restriction, either dietary or pharmacological, overcomes this resistance, offering a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Biomarker-guided responses in patient-derived organoids predict effective therapies in breast cancer
papers.summary: Bui et al. demonstrate that response-predictive models derived from patient biomarkers and clinical outcomes accurately predict in vitro responses in organoids using only biomarkers measurable in organoids as input and inform subtype-specific drug screening efforts. This highlights the potential of integrating organoids into personalized medicine strategies through gene-expression-based characterization.

papers.title: Universal catalytic endothelial lineage nanovesicles for targeting and rescuing ischemic endothelium
papers.summary: Jiang et al. present a dual-targeting nanovesicle platform armed with antioxidant nanozymes to treat ischemic diseases. By homing directly to injured endothelium, these engineered nanovesicles neutralize harmful reactive oxygen species and promote blood vessel regeneration, effectively repairing tissue damage across diverse rodent and large animal models.

papers.title: Gut commensal Olsenella profusa promotes endometriosis via lysophosphatidylcholine metabolite
papers.summary: Chen et al. show that gut commensal Olsenella profusa promotes endometriosis by producing LPC (16:0) via its phospholipase. LPC (16:0) activates the SPP1-PI3K-AKT pathway in endometrial stromal cells, driving lesion progression. These findings establish a gut microbe-metabolite-uterus axis and identify targets for diagnosis and therapy of endometriosis.

papers.title: An autonomous multimodal AI agent for evidence-grounded ophthalmic diagnosis
papers.summary: Zhao et al. present AgentEYE, a multimodal ophthalmic AI agent that routes fundus photographs and eye ultrasound images to specialized tools, retrieves clinical evidence, and generates traceable diagnostic reports. Retrospective benchmarks and blinded ophthalmologist review show improved report quality, safety, and citation grounding, supporting prospective validation.

papers.title: Corpora amylacea profiling reveals disease stage and brain region-specific alterations in glycogen metabolism in Alzheimer’s disease patient brains
papers.summary: Villareal and Bathe et al. studied glycogen metabolism in 230 patient brains with various neurodegenerative diseases. In Alzheimer’s disease patient brains, patch-like glycogen deposits were observed throughout the brain, which increased with disease severity. These findings strengthen the argument for an important role of glycogen metabolism in Alzheimer’s disease pathogenesis.

papers.title: Phase 1 study of intracranial T cell therapy with pemetrexed for refractory brain metastases and glioblastomas
papers.summary: Li et al. assess the safety and early efficacy of an intracranially autologous cell therapy combined with chemotherapy in patients with refractory brain metastases and glioblastomas, demonstrating tolerability alongside preliminary efficacy signals. Exploratory cerebrospinal fluid analyses reveal treatment-associated immune activation and tumor dynamics, offering early biological rationale for the strategy.

papers.title: Clinical landscape of human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte therapy
papers.summary: Heart failure destroys heart muscle cells that the body cannot replace. Stem cell therapies aim to change that. This review covers recent clinical trials testing human pluripotent stem cell-derived heart muscle cells delivered as injections, patches, and spheroids and summarizes early results on their safety and efficacy.

papers.title: Leave No Data Behind: Exploring a new paradigm in oncology with foundation models and large language models
papers.summary: Foundation models and large language models are reshaping cancer AI by integrating imaging, electronic health records, molecular profiles, and other oncology data. In this review, Corso et al. introduce “Leave No Data Behind” and examines the evidence, opportunities, and challenges for translating these models into clinical oncology.

papers.title: Iparomlimab and tuvonralimab in previously treated patients with cervical cancer
papers.summary: Lou et al. report results from a multi-center single-arm phase 2 trial showing that iparomlimab and tuvonralimab (QL1706) yields promising efficacy and well-tolerable safety in previously treated patients with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer. The high antitumor activity is irrespective of the PD-L1 status, histologic type, or prior bevacizumab treatment.

papers.title: Capsid inclusion in a CHIKV mRNA vaccine impairs adaptive immune responses
papers.summary: Chen et al. reveal that antigen architecture may determine immune fate following CHIKV mRNA vaccination. Capsid-deleted V2 promotes sustained B cell differentiation, Th1-biased T cell responses, and superior protection, whereas capsid-containing V1 impairs recognition of E2/E1 epitopes. These findings establish a framework for rational antigen engineering of alphavirus mRNA vaccines.

papers.title: Tumor-distal mediastinal lymph nodes harbor tumor-related progenitor exhausted T cells in lung cancer after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy
papers.summary: Zhang et al. show that in lung squamous cell carcinoma after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, tumor-distal mediastinal lymph nodes resemble tumor-proximal nodes and harbor functional progenitor exhausted CD8+ T cells clonally linked to tumor-infiltrating exhausted T cells, highlighting tdMLNs as potential antitumor immune reservoirs.

papers.title: EGFR inhibition promotes functional engraftment and graft survival via donor-derived CHI3L1 in fetal RPE suspension transplantation
papers.summary: Mao et al. show that transplanted donor RPE cells enter an early EGFR-dependent maladaptive state and that erlotinib treatment redirects them toward epithelial reintegration through CHI3L1-IL13RA2 signaling. Erlotinib also reshapes the local innate immune niche and improves donor-cell survival in immunocompetent models.

papers.title: Early-life immune imprinting by a B. infantis-HMO synbiotic shapes infant immune signatures and protects against experimental respiratory disease
papers.summary: Rashid et al. report that an infant-type Bifidobacterium infantis-HMO synbiotic shapes immune signatures and reduces Th2 bias in formula-fed infants toward a breastfed-like profile. In experimental models, it protects against bronchiolitis and confers lasting immune effects into adulthood, associated with increased 12-HHT, a lipid mediator sufficient to promote disease tolerance.

papers.title: Targeting Gi/o-coupled GPCRs to inhibit nociceptors: Insights from the serotonin receptor Htr1b and triptans
papers.summary: Peng et al. develop a preclinical screening platform that identifies Gi/o-coupled and orphan GPCRs enriched in CGRP+ mouse and human DRG neurons. Using Htr1b and triptans as proof of principle, they show that activating Gi/o-coupled GPCRs attenuates nociceptor excitability and reduces specific pain-related behaviors in mice.

papers.title: Köhlmeier-Degos disease is an interferonopathy characterized by type I and II interferon-driven inflammatory vasculopathy
papers.summary: Cudrici et al. examine inflammatory vascular injury in Köhlmeier-Degos disease. Single-cell profiling of skin, blood, and cerebrospinal fluid reveals type I and II interferon activation and cytotoxic T cell involvement, while ruxolitinib treatment in one patient is associated with suppression of interferon programs.

papers.title: An antibody-PROTAC conjugate targets BRD4/c-Myc/PD-L1 to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.summary: Gu et al. develop ASA, an antibody-PROTAC conjugate for TNBC, that integrates tumor homing, hypoxia-responsive cleavage, and PROTAC-mediated degradation. This design enables targeted degradation within tumors and promotes robust antitumor immunity and long-term immune memory when combined with αPD-L1.

papers.title: Persistent cytolytic CD8+ T cells recognize SARS-CoV-2 and herpesvirus epitopes in long COVID
papers.summary: Ma et al. perform deep-phenotyping of CD8+ T cells specific for viruses implicated in LC pathogenesis: SARS-CoV-2, CMV, and EBV. These T cells from LC individuals share features of terminal differentiation, activation, exhaustion, and cytolysis. The inability to dampen acute-phase cytolytic viral-specific CD8+ T cell responses may be an LC feature.

papers.title: Tumor-induced dendritic cell deregulation perturbs T cell proliferation and predicts clinical outcome in acute lymphoblastic leukemia
papers.summary: Kumar et al. show that specialization of dendritic cells (DCs) into distinct functional subsets is disrupted in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). This disruption impairs the ability of DCs to prime T cells. DC phenotype in patient peripheral blood and bone marrow at ALL presentation is an indicator of their prognosis.

papers.title: Parent-of-origin effects in Alzheimer’s liability dissociate neurocognitive and cardiovascular traits in at-risk individuals
papers.summary: Savignac et al. show that parent-of-origin effects in Alzheimer’s disease extend beyond a classic gender-by-lineage model and instead reflect a complex, context-dependent genetic architecture. They identify and characterize three genetically anchored intermediate phenotypes, which display unique and spatially distributed gender and lineage biases across the brain and phenome.

papers.title: Real-time AR navigation with dynamic tracking for millimeter-level pulmonary nodule localization: A randomized clinical trial
papers.summary: Huang et al. compare real-time augmented-reality navigation with CT guidance for preoperative localization of small peripheral pulmonary nodules. In this randomized trial, AR guidance shows noninferior accuracy; reduces radiation exposure, procedure time, and needle adjustments; and maintains a safety profile comparable to CT guidance.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases
papers.summary: Calina and Grafenhorst et al. using DNA methylation profiling of mucinous ovarian tumors characterize two mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) subgroups with potential differing outcomes and describe epigenetic patterns consistent with the stepwise relationship between mucinous borderline ovarian tumor and MOC. An epigenetic classifier accurately distinguishes MOC from metastases, improving diagnosis.

papers.title: Therapeutic Gfral silencing via antisense oligonucleotides ameliorates cancer-associated cachexia and extends survival in tumor-bearing mice
papers.summary: Hong et al. demonstrate that silencing central GFRAL using an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) reverses cancer-associated cachexia. In severe tumor models, a single central administration of the ASO mitigates muscle and adipose wasting, improves functional strength, and profoundly extends survival, highlighting receptor-targeted ASO therapy as a promising cachexia intervention.

papers.title: CRISPR-Cas9-producing probiotic bacteria for editing NOX2/gp91phox and treating inflammatory bowel disease
papers.summary: Zhang et al. prepare EcN-RNP hydrogel, aiming to treat IBD by inhibiting NOX2 expression via CRISPR-Cas9-mediated genome editing. The hydrogel enhances oxidative stress defense pathways and modulates glutamate and proline metabolism to reduce ROS.

papers.title: Combine antibody-drug conjugate with cmLumiOpto for triple-negative breast cancer treatment
papers.summary: Varadkar et al. show that combining a targeted antibody-drug conjugate with mitochondria-disrupting gene therapy shrinks tumors, halts metastasis, and activates the immune system in preclinical models with low toxicity, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for aggressive triple-negative breast cancer.

papers.title: Driving tumor-associated macrophages to a CXCL9Hi/SPP1Low phenotype eliminates pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: Immunosuppressive CXCL9Lo/SPP1Hi myeloid cells are highly abundant in PDAC, adding to the poor prognosis. Using the myeloid cell-targeting cyclodextrin nanoconstruct, Nguyen et al. found that simultaneously modulating CXCL9 and SPP1 through this single, systemically administered nanoformulation is highly effective in treating murine PDAC.

papers.title: A biomimetic hybrid membrane vesicle nanoplatform attenuates tendinopathy through neuroinflammation modulation and tendon regeneration
papers.summary: Li et al. develop an integrated nanoplatform for tendinopathy. The platform buffers inflammatory cytokines and pain-related neuropeptides, alleviates tendon stem/progenitor cell senescence, and improves tendon remodeling, pain behaviors, and function in rats.

papers.title: Self-sufficient killing of malignant tumors by an engineered cancer-selective gene circuit
papers.summary: Liu et al. present a synthetic cancer-selective promoter (PETS∗) that converts the aberrant expression profiles of ETS family transcription factors (e.g., amplification or gene fusion) into tumor-restricted gene expression in vivo, enabling self-sufficient elimination of malignant cells, while sparing fast-proliferating healthy tissues following adenovirus delivery.

papers.title: Combination of exosome vaccines, lenvatinib, and anti-PD-1 eradicates tumor in autochthonous hepatocellular carcinoma mice
papers.summary: Zuo et al. show that a dendritic cell-derived exosome vaccine combined with lenvatinib enhances intratumoral antigen presentation and T cell priming, while anti-PD-1 overcomes T cell exhaustion. This triple combination eradicates established autochthonous hepatocellular carcinoma in mice and generates durable antitumor immunity.

papers.title: A poly(I:C)/QS-21-based in situ vaccine synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to overcome tumor immunoresistance
papers.summary: Zhang et al. demonstrate that the combination of QS-21 and poly(I:C) facilitates the endosomal escape of poly(I:C) and enhances immunogenic cell death, thereby functioning as an in situ vaccine that potentiates CD8+T cell-mediated antitumor immunity and overcomes resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy.

papers.title: Efficacy and biomarker exploration of anlotinib plus penpulimab in second-line ES-SCLC: Results from the phase 2 ALTER-L041 trial
papers.summary: Zeng et al. show that combining penpulimab and anlotinib provides promising antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile in patients with platinum-resistant extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. This phase 2 trial suggests that this combination serves as a viable second-line treatment option.

papers.title: Fatty-acid-based antimiR-23b delivery in the DMSXL model: A potential therapeutic strategy for brain dysfunction in myotonic dystrophy type 1
papers.summary: Piqueras-Losilla et al. show that the fatty-acid-conjugated antimiR-23b X82108 reaches the brain after systemic administration in mice and non-human primates. X82108 increases MBNL1/2 levels, reduces toxic DMPK transcripts, corrects DM1-associated splicing defects, and improves behavioral abnormalities, resulting in broad correction of CNS defects in DMSXL mice.

papers.title: Nilotinib induces immunogenic cuproptosis to potentiate cancer immunotherapy
papers.summary: Yao et al. identify nilotinib, an FDA-approved anti-tumor drug, as a non-ionophore immunogenic cuproptosis inducer that potentiates anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Mechanistically, nilotinib-copper represses ATP7A via ETV1 to drive mitochondrial copper accumulation and activates ERK2 phosphorylation to potentiate cuproptosis.

papers.title: Association of residential greenness and Life’s Essential 8 with cardiovascular disease in China
papers.summary: Cao et al. reveal the effects of residential greenness and Life’s Essential 8 on cardiovascular disease in China. Greenness exposure and higher Life’s Essential 8 scores are associated with better cardiovascular health, highlighting the importance of both green infrastructure and healthy lifestyles in reducing cardiovascular risk in rapidly urbanizing China.

papers.title: Retrieval-augmented generation in medicine: A scoping review of technical implementations, clinical applications, and ethical considerations
papers.summary: Yang et al. review 251 studies of RAG in medicine, summarizing technical implementations, clinical applications, and ethical considerations. They identify limited evaluation of bias and safety, insufficient attention to equity, and key priorities for enabling responsible global deployment of medical RAG.

papers.title: Spinal cord stimulation modulates post-synaptic inhibition to improve arm neuromotor control after chronic stroke
papers.summary: Borda et al. demonstrate that epidural spinal cord stimulation enhances inhibitory circuit function, improving arm reaching kinematics in individuals with post-stroke hemiparesis. Their findings provide new insight into the spinal circuits influenced by SCS and support its potential as a neurotechnology to promote motor recovery after stroke.

papers.title: Programmable-bacteria-macrophage backpacks for enhanced solid tumor therapy via mechanobiological interplay
papers.summary: In brief, Fan et al. develop a programmable-bacteria-macrophage system in which ultrasound (US)-triggered thermal stimulation induces bacterial lysis and therapeutic payload release. This process promotes macrophage repolarization toward the CD86-expressing phenotype within the tumor microenvironment, enhances immune cell infiltration, and highlights the role of tumor-cell mechanobiological properties in immunotherapy.

papers.title: Bristol Myers wins ‘milestone’ FDA approval of myeloma drug acquired from Celgene
papers.summary: The clearance of Zenbexus is the first for a group of protein-degrading “CELMoD” medicines that could help Bristol Myers rejuvenate a key drug franchise.

papers.title: Capricor shares spike on CEO comments; Cytokinetics sues Bristol Myers
papers.summary: The FDA is “willing to review” an updated submission for Capricor’s Duchenne cell therapy, its CEO said. Elsewhere, a heart drug battle spilled into court and Rigel priced the first “Protac” medicine.

papers.title: Biotech initiatives pick up as more regions race to become hubs
papers.summary: New government funding from Pennsylvania to Kansas City is strengthening biotech hubs — but experts say money alone won’t determine where pharma builds next.

papers.title: New Taiho, Cullinan data heats up lung cancer drug battle
papers.summary: The findings position their drug, zipalertinib, as a threat to multiple approved medicines — while setting a bar for others in testing.

papers.title: PTC takes a chance on Sangamo’s Fabry disease gene therapy
papers.summary: Wall Street analysts view the deal as a risky, high-reward bet on a treatment that’s nearing a possible regulatory approval and could be superior to existing medications.

papers.title: Lilly files six lawsuits in bid to shut down ‘black market’ for retatrutide
papers.summary: Ahead of an approval filing, the drugmaker is amping up a fight against sellers who claim to offer versions of its highly anticipated “triple-G” weight loss medicine.

papers.title: Psychedelics developer Definium scores more positive data for LSD pill
papers.summary: Results from a late-stage study focused on generalized anxiety disorder were a “clean win” to analysts, who believe Definium has a drug with multibillion-dollar sales potential.

papers.title: Silence cashes in on ‘differentiated’ data; UK reaffirms support for childhood vaccines
papers.summary: Some analysts believe Silence’s polycythemia vera drug could be superior to a closely watched Takeda medicine. Elsewhere, the FDA spurned a radiopharmaceutical and AbCellera shares climbed to levels not seen since 2023.

papers.title: Boulevard starts up with $65M to pursue targeted autoimmune drugs
papers.summary: Co-founded by pioneering researcher Georg Schett and ex-Sanofi CSO Frank Nestle, the startup is advancing a trio of multifaceted antibodies with the potential to treat several immune diseases.

papers.title: Ex-Legend CEO takes helm at biotech startup scouring the globe for drugs
papers.summary: Ying Huang is now running K2 Therapeutics, which has licensed multiple prospects from China-based biotechs and is searching for more “high-potential” medicines.

Skye Bioscience has entered into an agreement to combine with privately held fibrotic disease biotech Redx Pharma in a deal that will net $125 million in financing for the new public company, called Fibrx Therapeutics.

Capricor Therapeutics has bounced back from a bruising FDA advisory committee meeting by securing a green light to file an amendment to its approval application, raising hopes that the biotech can rescue its Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy. The biotech’s stock soared following the news.
BioCryst CEO Charlie Gayer told Fierce the company is “not getting away from science and R&D” despite shutting down its internal discovery efforts.

Just weeks after Legend Biotech announced the departure of its CEO, Ying Huang, K2 Therapeutics has announced that Wang will now lead the startup, which was founded in 2024 with a $50 million seed round from MPM BioImpact.
Despite mixed results for its experimental schizophrenia treatment last month, MapLight Therapeutics is going all-in on the asset—at the expense of its preclinical programs.
PDS Biotechnology has called a halt to its phase 3 head and neck cancer therapy to channel resources to a drug in phase 2 development for metastatic colorectal cancer.
With the post-IPO quiet period having come to an end, CEO Benny Sørensen, M.D., Ph.D., was free to sit down with Fierce to map out Hemab’s future.
Three years after Robert Hoffman sold XinThera to Gilead, the veteran Pfizer chemist has unveiled his latest venture.
After 15 years with Medtronic’s structural heart franchise, Bill Shields is leaving the medtech giant to become the chief executive of startup Versa Vascular.

PTC Therapeutics has struck a deal to buy Sangamo Therapeutics’ Fabry disease program for $111 million upfront, outbidding Astellas and TerSera Therapeutics for the near-approval gene therapy. Sangamo, selling assets as part of its bankruptcy proceedings, also offloaded technology to Eli Lilly for $50 million.

Taiho Pharmaceutical and Cullinan Therapeutics have celebrated a second phase 3 victory for their small-molecule EGFR inhibitor, teeing up the partners to challenge Johnson & Johnson in a lung cancer niche.
As the FDA mulls whether to approve Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics’ rusfertide, Zealand Pharma has sold its own rights to the blood cancer drug in return for $100 million.

A new analysis from the Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development (CSDD) found that an AI clinical monitoring agent can deliver an estimated 82-fold return on investment in phase 3 oncology trials.
The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

Aardvark Therapeutics has confirmed it is walking away from recently terminated phase 3 trials, telling investors it has no plans to resume the studies “as previously designed” as it works to find a path forward for its stalled pipeline.
The FDA gave Samsung Electronics the go-ahead for the latest software features that allow its Galaxy Buds earphones to act as an OTC hearing aid that also allows users to diagnose their hearing.
Definium Therapeutics’ LSD formula has gone two for two in its phase 3 program, notching a win in generalized anxiety disorder months after knocking a depression study out of the park.
Boulevard Bio has strolled out of stealth with $65 million in funding from Deerfield Management and three autoimmune disease candidates.
CytoDyn's leronlimab may have struggled to secure approval as an HIV treatment, but research in infant primates has offered fresh hope for the CCR5-targeting antibody's ability to treat the virus.
Amgen is expanding its footprint in India with an R&D center in Hyderabad, the latest by from the California company to boost its research facilities.

Epicrispr Biotechnologies has raised $90 million in a series C round backed by investors including Sanofi Ventures, positioning the biotech to advance a pipeline of epigenetic medicines led by an early-phase facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy prospect.
Sentynl Therapeutics has penned a deal potentially worth $475 million for the option to market Mereo BioPharma's phase 3-ready rare genetic respiratory disease drug in the U.S.
As always, if you know of layoffs occurring at a biotech, please reach out to the Fierce Biotech editorial team.
Two giants of their respective fields, Abbott and Google, are joining forces for a first-of-its-kind team-up that aims to build out a digital picture of people’s health.
Aura Biosciences is refocusing under its recently installed CEO, laying off 20% of its employees and overhauling its C-suite as it narrows its focus on ocular oncology.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01292-y Wang et al. design efficient robot–environment interaction representations that achieve generalization across articulated robotic hand models and task adaptability in diverse cluttered grasping scenarios, suggesting a path towards general-purpose robotics.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01280-2 Johnson et al. demonstrate an autonomous three-bar tensegrity robot capable of robust locomotion across varied terrains even after extreme impacts, including a 5.7-m drop onto asphalt.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 05 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01275-z A new deep learning method enables molecular dynamics simulations over longer time scales while still achieving accurate physical property prediction.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning steers generative crystal design
papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 03 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01282-0 Generative machine learning methods have led to progress in crystal discovery, but cannot fully explore the space of material candidates that are both novel and useful. A reinforcement learning-based method steers candidate generation to these areas, enabling the design of novel functional materials.

papers.summary: Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 03 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01278-w Xiao et al. show that large language models partially align with human brain activity during deductive reasoning. papers.summary: Mederacke et al. show that the lung’s fractal bronchial tree emerges through fluid-structure interactions that equalize mechanical stresses across all branches. These developmental principles continue to operate throughout life. Key biophysical parameters change in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, offering potential biomarkers for diagnosis.

papers.summary: Atsavapranee et al. present a microfluidic platform that accurately quantifies unfolding kinetics for many proteins in parallel. After expressing and immobilizing EGFP-tagged variants within device chambers, introducing the thermolysin protease drives protein cleavage as they unfold. Monitoring the loss of EGFP over time via microscopy quantifies unfolding rates while using minimal reagents.

papers.summary: Wang et al. show that oscillatory phase-separated condensates enhance TTFL clock robustness by separating translation enhancement from transcriptional repression. Modeling and knockdown experiments support a hybrid architecture in which condensates retain intrinsic rhythmicity while being tuned by the core TTFL.

papers.title: Delineation of signaling microdomains from live-cell movies
papers.summary: A computational method identifies subcellular signaling microdomains from live-cell movies. The detected microdomains reveal distinct spatiotemporal organization in the signaling of canonical Rho GTPases and GEFs and are sensitive to optogenetic perturbation.

papers.title: Evaluating SARS-CoV-2 antibody resilience via prediction and design of escape viral variants

By experimentally validating functional, highly mutated proteins, this model identifies vulnerabilities in therapeutic antibodies and quantifies cocktail synergy against future viral evolution.

papers.summary: Although metabolomics has shown considerable promise for biomarker discovery, and the development of diagnostic and prognostic applications, its translation into routine clinical practice remains limited by analytical complexity, cost, throughput, and standardization challenges. papers.title: Mining Microbial Transcriptomes to Engineer Cell-Based Bacterial Biosensors in Gut-Resident Bacteroidaceae
papers.summary: The gastrointestinal tract is rich in metabolic, immune, and microbiome-derived signals that can inform the design of live biotherapeutics and diagnosis of intestinal disorders. papers.summary: Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) are actin-supported membrane bridges that mediate long-range intercellular communication and direct transfer of signaling molecules, organelles, and pathogenic cargo, yet the physicochemical mechanisms underlying their formation and organization remain poorly understood. papers.summary: Genomic recording enables transient biological signals to be indelibly captured through DNA alterations, creating a permanent record of cellular history retrievable by sequencing. papers.summary: Aberrant protein-protein interactions (PPIs) drive myriad diseases. Inhibiting these PPIs often relies on discovering molecules that bind to one of the proteins and hoping that this binding inhibits the PPI. Molecular binder discovery often takes months, but a discovery process that ensures that the resulting molecule not only binds a target protein, but selectively inhibits a target PPI, could dramatically accelerate these endeavors. papers.summary: Abstract MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short noncoding RNAs that post–transcriptionally regulate gene expression. papers.summary: Abstract Small RNAs (sRNAs) rarely cause strong growth phenotypes upon overexpression, complicating efforts to link regulatory interactions to physiological outcomes. papers.summary: Abstract 3D structure of the chromatin is crucial for cell identity and gene regulation. papers.summary: Abstract Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) modifications cluster around the peptidyl transferase centre (PTC), the catalytic centre of the ribosome, yet their collective functional roles remain unclear. papers.summary: Abstract Accurate predictions of DNA-binding residues (DBRs) in protein sequences facilitate decoding molecular-level mechanisms underlying cellular functions that involve protein–DNA interactions. papers.summary: Abstract Delineating the constituents and structural composition of RNA-associated protein complexes is essential to mapping the molecular machinery driving RNA metabolism and its impact on cellular function. papers.summary: Abstract Sparsomycin (SPA) is a broad-spectrum inhibitor of protein synthesis with activity across all three domains of life. papers.summary: Abstract RNase P is primarily responsible for processing the 5′ end of precursor transfer RNA (tRNA). papers.summary: Abstract Epigenetic inheritance relies on the precise recycling of parental histones during DNA replication. papers.summary: Abstract Studying the fine-scale dynamics of telomere replication has been hindered by the heterogeneity of native telomeres and the limitations of existing tools. papers.summary: Abstract Cross-species transmission of mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses (MBFVs) relies on multi-host switching and adaptation, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. papers.summary: Abstract Bacteriophage genomes exhibit exceptional diversity in nucleotide modifications, which primarily function to counteract host defense systems. papers.summary: Abstract Polymerase theta-mediated end-joining (TMEJ) is a stand-alone mutagenic DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair pathway that becomes critical when high-fidelity repair is compromised. papers.summary: Abstract The clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 system has become a powerful genome-editing tool that uses RNA–DNA pairing to cleave target DNA with protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequences. papers.summary: Abstract During bacterial ribosome recycling, 70S ribosomes are split into subunits by ribosome recycling factor (RRF) and elongation factor G (EF-G). papers.summary: Abstract Replication stress threatens genome integrity by stalling replication forks, which may lead to double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) breaks. papers.title: The ZN domain acts as a dynamic switch coordinating multiple-step aminoacylation in bacterial leucyl-tRNA synthetase
papers.summary: Abstract Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases (AARSs) safeguard translational fidelity by coordinating amino acid activation and tRNA charging within distinct catalytic and editing domains. In leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS), the small, centrally located zinc-binding domain (ZN domain) sits at the crossroads of these functional centres, yet its role has remained enigmatic. Here, we present crystal structures of the Escherichia coli LeuRS–tRNA Leu complex that capture the ZN domain in a previously unobserved conformation, revealing the pre-activation state. By integrating structural data with kinetic analysis, we propose a model for the aminoacylation reaction in which the ZN domain functions as a dynamic molecular switch that coordinates the different catalytic steps of the reaction cycle. We show that the ZN domain first acts as a wedge to prime the synthetic active site while locking the 3′-end tRNA Leu in the editing domain. papers.title: Toy-inspired bioengineering
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 14 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00491-x Bioengineers can repurpose the underlying physical principles of classic toys to create highly effective, ultra-low-cost biomedical tools. Embracing this frugality can democratize cutting-edge science and increase the accessibility of healthcare in low-resource settings.

papers.title: Sustainable cold-chain technology
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00483-x Cold chains are essential to food security and global health. At NanoFreeze, a Colombian start-up, we are developing a sustainable cold-chain preservation and energy-efficient refrigeration technology based on a bacterial ice-nucleation protein. Here, we reflect on how intellectual property, regulatory validation and strategic partnerships shaped our path from biological insight to translation in an emerging economy.

papers.title: Technology readiness is not clinical translation readiness
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00484-w Health technologies are typically judged by their technical maturity rather than their ability to improve patient care. As a result, many innovations achieve technological success but fail to reach routine clinical use. Here, we propose clinical translation readiness levels to assess whether health technologies are truly ready for adoption, implementation and patient benefit.

papers.title: Antifibrotic biomaterials
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 13 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00489-5 Fibrosis is a major cause of organ dysfunction and mortality, yet current therapies rarely reverse established disease. Biomaterials offer new opportunities to locally modulate tissue-specific repair environments and guide healing away from scar formation and toward regeneration.

papers.title: Rehabilitation beyond prosthetics in wartime Ukraine
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 12 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00486-8 Ukraine is experiencing an unprecedented burden of major limb loss within a health system strained by war. As an expert in prosthetics and neurorehabilitation and full-time volunteer in wartime Ukraine, I share my experience of how recovery extends beyond prosthetic technology alone and depends on appropriate and timely care, continuity of rehabilitation, and trained personnel. Bioengineering influences not only devices but also how care is delivered under constrained conditions.

papers.title: Human disease models by design
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 11 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00473-z Human cell-based 3D models hold promise for preclinical research as new approach methodologies, but realizing their translational potential will require moving beyond legacy culture systems and towards bioengineering-guided design to improve reproducibility, scalability and relevance.

papers.title: Acoustofluidics for translational medicine
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 10 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00479-7 Acoustofluidics is emerging as a versatile platform for clinical diagnostics and therapy, enabling real-time, label-free sensing, manipulation and control of biological and chemical systems across scales. This Review discusses translational progress across key medical workflows, highlights challenges in standardization and integration, and outlines pathways from proof-of-concept devices to clinically deployable systems.

papers.title: Human-centred design
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 07 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00475-x Design failures often result not from technical flaws but from a lack of consideration into how, why and by whom a technology will be used. Human-centred design prioritizes collaboration with user communities to develop adoptable technologies, ultimately saving time and resources.
